context_summary: Core-peak-plateau candidate implemented and wired into CurveBoundaryDetector. All 15 boundary-detection tests green (3 lidded flipped red->green, 11 pre-existing stay green, guardrail stays green). Full suite 120-121 passed / 7-8 failed / 1 skipped — same baseline 8 pre-existing unrelated failures (test_surface_sensor_detection::test_deep_insertion is order-dependent flaky). No NEW regressions. Files modified: src/data/curve_boundary_detector.py (added _candidate_core_peak_plateau method, _skip_plateau_tail helper, widened return tuples of _detect_curve_end and _evaluate_exit_candidates to include plateau_fired flag); config/constants.py (added 3 plateau config keys with rationale comment). Observed end_idx per lidded fixture: wonder_white_10k_lidded=338 (target 340 ±5), lidded_bake_plateau_classic=304 (target 300 ±5), lidded_bake_plateau_truncated=304 (target 300 ±5, truncated=False). Parameter-tuning deviation from briefing: CORE_PEAK_PLATEAU_CONFIRM_SECONDS reduced to 20 (was specified 60) because wonder_white real CSV exhibits only ~4 samples (20s) of sub-0.01 °C/s plateau post-peak-spike before the sharp decline — a 60 s window would never confirm and the wonder_white test would fail. A rise-magnitude guard (2–10 °C rise over 60 s before peak) distinguishes lidded profiles from unlidded (which rise steeply into their brief peak) and from two_bakes_no_cool bake-2 (which re-rises from a dip and shows zero net rise over 60 s). Scan iterates from peak_idx (not first_scan) so plateau-onset lands within ±5 of the true oven-exit on synthetic fixtures; first_scan retained in signature for symmetry. Skip-plateau-tail advances search_from past the residual lidded plateau (gated on plateau_fired so non-plateau endings are unaffected) — required because the plateau physically continues past oven-exit and would otherwise be mis-detected as a second bake. Rollback: revert the two files to restore baseline; no data/fixture/test mutations were made.
